s1.syndrome_frame: Palpitations with tachycardia and abnormal atrial activation
salient_findings: Positive P waves in leads II, III, aVF, and V₁
Counterclockwise propagation around the mitral annulus and left atrial appendage
Low-voltage scar at the prior mitral isthmus line
key_facts: 78-year-old woman
History of two prior catheter ablations for persistent atrial fibrillation
Presented with palpitations
12-lead ECG showed an atrial cycle length of 280 ms
Positive P waves in leads II, III, aVF, and V₁
Electroanatomic activation map demonstrated counterclockwise propagation
Low-voltage scar at the prior mitral isthmus line
Entrainment pacing revealed postpacing intervals within 20 ms of the tachycardia cycle length at certain locations
Postpacing interval more than 20 ms longer than the cycle length when pacing adjacent to the mitral isthmus scar
Activation within the vein of Marshall matched the tachycardia cycle length

shortlist.label: Macroreentrant Atrial Tachycardia
shortlist.why_kept: Counterclockwise propagation around the mitral annulus and left atrial appendage

shortlist.label: Mitral Isthmus Dependent Atrial Flutter
shortlist.why_kept: Low-voltage scar at the prior mitral isthmus line and entrainment pacing results

shortlist.label: Vein of Marshall Epicardial Tachycardia
shortlist.why_kept: Activation within the vein of Marshall matched the tachycardia cycle length

shortlist.label: Scar Mediated Atrial Tachycardia
shortlist.why_kept: Presence of a low-voltage scar at the prior mitral isthmus line

shortlist.label: Perimitral Reentrant Tachycardia
shortlist.why_kept: Propagation around the mitral annulus and interruption by a low-voltage scar

raw.rationale: The activation within the vein of Marshall matched the tachycardia cycle length, suggesting an epicardial pathway bypassing the scar, which is consistent with Vein of Marshall Epicardial Tachycardia

rejected.label: Macroreentrant Atrial Tachycardia
rejected.why: While the electroanatomic activation map showed counterclockwise propagation, the specific involvement of the vein of Marshall points more towards a localized epicardial pathway

rejected.label: Mitral Isthmus Dependent Atrial Flutter
rejected.why: The presence of a low-voltage scar at the prior mitral isthmus line and the postpacing interval more than 20 ms longer than the cycle length when pacing adjacent to the mitral isthmus scar suggest the mitral isthmus is not the primary pathway

rejected.label: Scar Mediated Atrial Tachycardia
rejected.why: While there is a low-voltage scar, the key finding of activation within the vein of Marshall matching the tachycardia cycle length indicates the tachycardia is more related to the epicardial pathway than just scar mediation

rejected.label: Perimitral Reentrant Tachycardia
rejected.why: The evidence of an epicardial pathway bypassing the scar, specifically involving the vein of Marshall, makes Perimitral Reentrant Tachycardia less likely as it typically involves reentry around the mitral annulus without specifying epicardial involvement
